project.title: Antibiotic resistance genes and their bacterial hosts in bioelectrochemically treated hospital wastewater
project.description: Hospital wastewater contains a complex mixture of pharmaceuticals and antibiotic-resistant bacteria, posing challenges for conventional and advanced treatment technologies. This project investigates the microbial community composition and antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) dynamics in hospital wastewater treated using a fixed-bed bioelectrochemical reactor (FBER), compared with a non-electrochemical open-circuit voltage (OCV) control. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed on inoculum, biofilm, and effluent samples collected throughout 128 days of reactor operation under continuous pharmaceutical exposure, enabling both community-level taxonomic and functional profiling, as well as the recovery of metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) to resolve ARG-host identity, virulence factors, and mobile genetic element associations.
